title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
claim: Bright Ln3+ emission with quantum yields above about 50% generally requires ligand antenna sensitization rather than direct 4f–4f excitation, with the ligand–metal energy gap matched to the target ion and high-energy oscillators kept out of the coordination sphere.
explanation: Parity-forbidden 4f–4f transitions have very small absorption coefficients and long lifetimes. High-energy OH, NH, and CH oscillators quench the excited states, so chromophoric ligands should harvest light, transfer energy (typically via the ligand triplet), and form a rigid protective shell. The Dieke diagram differs between ions, so the ligand excited-state energy must be tuned to the emitting level.
scope: Molecular Ln3+ complexes intended as luminescent materials, including luminescent SMMs.
conditions: Indirect excitation through ligand chromophores; suppression of non-radiative paths from inner- and outer-sphere OH, NH, and CH oscillators.
caveats: Direct f–f excitation remains possible but rarely gives highly luminescent materials. A direct singlet-to-Ln energy transfer is described as much less probable than the singlet–triplet–Ln route.
